title: Choose One Operating Principle for the Year
teaser: A new year can begin with one useful rule instead of a crowded list of ambitions.
full_text: Write one principle that could simplify decisions throughout the year. Make it behavioral enough to use, such as finishing fewer things well or reviewing commitments every Friday.

title: Build the First Week Around Real Capacity
teaser: Early-year enthusiasm can make a calendar look more spacious than it is.
full_text: Mark the fixed demands of the next seven days before adding new goals. Put new work only into the time that actually remains.

title: Stress-Test a Decision in Reverse
teaser: Asking when a good-looking choice could fail helps expose conditions you may be overlooking.
full_text: Take one decision you are considering and write: Under what circumstances would this be the wrong choice? Add the most credible answer to your decision process.

title: Remove One Repeated Point of Friction
teaser: A tiny obstacle that appears every day can become a meaningful monthly cost.
full_text: Find one recurring task and remove a needless step. A shortcut, template, better placement, or clearer default is enough.

title: Write the Purpose Before a Difficult Conversation
teaser: Conversations drift more easily when nobody is clear about what needs to be resolved.
full_text: Before an important conversation today, write its purpose in one sentence. Use that sentence to return to the issue if the discussion wanders.

title: Measure Your Open Loops, Not Your Motivation
teaser: Mental fatigue can come from too many unfinished commitments rather than a lack of ambition.
full_text: List the tasks currently taking up mental space. Finish, delegate, schedule properly, or deliberately drop at least one of them.

title: Trace One Claim Back to Its Source
teaser: Repeating an idea is different from knowing what its original evidence actually says.
full_text: Choose one claim that matters to a decision you are making. Find the earliest reliable source you can and check its date, context, and exact conclusion.

title: Turn a Goal Into a Repeatable Behavior
teaser: A broad goal is difficult to follow when it never tells you what action counts today.
full_text: Convert one goal into a behavior with a time, frequency, or measurable action. Replace an aspiration with something you can actually schedule.

title: Ask Instead of Guessing an Expectation
teaser: Unspoken expectations can create unnecessary work and avoidable resentment.
full_text: In one unclear task or relationship, ask what is actually expected. Clarify the deadline, boundary, responsibility, or outcome that has been left implicit.

title: Shrink an Unfinished Task Until It Can Start
teaser: When the whole project feels heavy, the next physical action can be much smaller.
full_text: Choose something you have postponed and reduce it to a step you could begin in ten minutes. Complete only that step today.

title: Look at Frequency, Not Just the Price
teaser: A small expense can matter because of how often it repeats, not because any single purchase is large.
full_text: Pick one recurring small expense and estimate its annual frequency. Keep it if the total still feels worthwhile; otherwise set a deliberate limit.

title: Leave a Next-Step Note Before You Stop
teaser: Returning to unfinished work is faster when you do not have to reconstruct where you left off.
full_text: Before closing a document or project today, leave one line stating the next concrete action. Make re-entry easy for your future self.

title: Extract the Usable Part of Criticism
teaser: Feedback does not have to be entirely right or entirely wrong to contain something useful.
full_text: Take one criticism you received and separate it from its tone. Is there one concrete, testable point that could improve the work? Keep that part.

title: Move the Distraction Instead of Fighting It
teaser: Changing the environment can be more reliable than asking willpower to win the same battle repeatedly.
full_text: Add one step of distance between you and a frequent distraction today. Move the app, mute the alert, or put the object out of immediate reach.

title: Define an Early Warning Signal
teaser: A problem is easier to address when you know what small signal appears before it becomes expensive.
full_text: For one ongoing plan, write three measurable warning signs such as delayed replies, rising error rates, or budget drift. Decide when you will review them.

title: Schedule Rest Before the Calendar Fills
teaser: Rest that exists only if everything else finishes early is easy to postpone indefinitely.
full_text: Reserve one genuine rest period this week. Decide what needs to be completed beforehand so you are less tempted to convert it back into work.

title: Define a Boundary as Your Own Action
teaser: A useful boundary says what you will do, not how you will force someone else to behave.
full_text: Write one boundary for a recurring situation in the form: If this happens, I will do this. Keep the action within your control.

title: Write the Definition of Done Before Starting
teaser: Work can expand through extra detail when nobody has decided what completion actually means.
full_text: Before starting one task today, write the conditions that make it complete. Use them to challenge additions that appear later.

title: Check Whether an Old Note Is Still Current
teaser: Information can age quietly even when the document that contains it still looks trustworthy.
full_text: Open one old note, guide, or reference you use often. Check its date and verify one point that may have changed since it was written.

title: Name the Opportunity Cost
teaser: Every yes uses time, attention, or money that cannot be spent on another option.
full_text: For one meaningful choice, write two columns: what this option gives you and what it prevents or delays. Read both before deciding.

title: Make a Feedback Question Narrower
teaser: A broad question such as What do you think often produces feedback that is difficult to use.
full_text: Ask for feedback on one dimension today: clarity, speed, structure, tone, or risk. Give the other person a smaller target to evaluate.

title: Attach a Routine to a Clear Starting Cue
teaser: A habit is harder to repeat when its start time is renegotiated every day.
full_text: Choose a specific cue for one routine: after breakfast, when you arrive home, or when the first meeting ends. Let an existing event trigger the new action.

title: Sort the Mess Into Categories
teaser: Many small problems can feel like one impossible problem when they are never separated.
full_text: Group what is bothering you into a few categories such as time, money, people, information, or process. Work on one item from the densest category.

title: Connect a Good Result to the Process Behind It
teaser: Knowing what contributed to a success makes it easier to repeat than simply celebrating the outcome.
full_text: Think of something that went well recently. Identify one preparation, decision, or habit—apart from luck—that meaningfully contributed.

title: Add Buffer Between Commitments
teaser: Back-to-back plans allow one small delay to spill across the rest of the day.
full_text: Find one place in a busy schedule where two commitments touch. Add a short buffer and resist turning that buffer into another task.

title: Write the Use Case Before Buying
teaser: A product can feel necessary until you try to describe when you will actually use it.
full_text: Before one purchase today, write three realistic situations in which you would use it. If the scenarios remain vague, delay the decision.

title: Make a Request for Help Specific
teaser: Good intentions do not become useful support when the other person cannot tell what you need.
full_text: When asking for help today, state what you need, when you need it, and which part you will handle yourself.

title: Design the Minimum Version for a Bad Day
teaser: A routine that only works under ideal conditions may disappear exactly when life becomes demanding.
full_text: Choose one habit and define its minimum viable version for a very busy day. Keep the version small enough that it is genuinely sustainable.

title: Create a Signal That the Workday Is Over
teaser: Without a closing cue, unfinished work can continue occupying attention after you have stopped.
full_text: Choose one end-of-day action: write tomorrow's first task, close the workspace, or silence work notifications. Repeat it tonight.

title: Turn One Default Into a Deliberate Choice
teaser: Something you have done the same way for years may simply be a default, not the best current option.
full_text: Pick one routine default today and ask why it exists. If there is a plausible alternative, run a small, reversible experiment.

title: Close January With One Adjustment, Not a Verdict
teaser: A monthly review is more useful when it produces a practical change instead of a score about yourself.
full_text: Write three short notes for January: what worked, what created unnecessary strain, and what you will change in February. Carry only one adjustment forward.
